chunks: Hadith 4105 — Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:

I asked Abā Ibrāhīm عليه السلام about a man who has a pledged item in his possession, but does not know to whom among the people it belongs. He said: “I do not like that he sell it until its owner comes.”
I said: “He does not know to whom among the people it belongs.” He said: “Is there excess in it or deficiency?”

I said: “If there is excess in it or deficiency, what should he do?” He said: “If there is deficiency in it, then it is easier: he may sell it, and he will be rewarded for what remains. But if there is excess in it, then that is more difficult for him: he should sell it and keep its surplus until its owner comes.”

key_terms.الرَّهْنُ: a pledged item held as collateral
key_terms.فَضْلٌ: surplus or excess value beyond what is owed
key_terms.يُمْسِكُ فَضْلَهُ: he retains its surplus for the owner

ai.seo_question: What should be done with a pledged item when its owner is unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a pledged item whose owner is unknown. Imam Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام distinguishes between cases of deficiency and surplus value, instructing caution in disposing of the property and preservation of the owner's excess right until the owner appears.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4105 - Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
"I asked Abu Ibrahim (Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as)) about a man who has a pledged item (rahn) in his possession but does not know to whom it belongs.
Imam (as) said: 'I do not recommend that he sell it until its owner comes.'
I said: 'He does not know to whom it belongs.'
Imam (as) replied: 'Does it have any excess value or deficiency?'
I said: 'What if it has excess or deficiency, what should he do?'
Imam (as) said: 'If it has a deficiency, it is easier; he may sell it and be rewarded for what remains. However, if it has excess value, that is more difficult; he should sell it and hold the surplus until its owner comes.' "
